agent-action-surface.scfReason: Active agents expose write-capable Apex and Flow actions; the check counts them but does not measure what each task needs, so this is attack surface to review.
agent-action-surface.note: No HISO or NZISM citation: the check counts and classifies agent actions but does not measure what the agent task needs, and HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI.

agent-channel-exposure.scfReason: An active agent is reachable through a guest or public channel, so unauthenticated users can trigger agent actions that are not mapped to an authenticated identity, and the agent is not restricted to the channels it needs.

hsup.reason: Applies to an active agent bound to a guest-reachable site, embedded deployment or web messaging channel; the web application guidance requires 'only authorised personnel have access to information stored on the website', and the agent acts on org data for any visitor.

agent-channel-exposure.note: HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI and has no agent-specific requirement; the cited ids are the general access, design or logging requirements the finding evidences, applied to the agent as a non-human service identity.

agent-inventory.scfReason: An active agent runs as an inactive or frozen user, showing agent ownership and status are not tracked through the lifecycle and agent actions are not tied to a live, authorized identity.

hsup.reason: An active agent running as an inactive or frozen user shows 'the complete lifecycle of the account(s)' is not managed; the guidance names service accounts as a managed account type.

agent-inventory.note: HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI and has no agent-specific requirement; the cited ids are the general access, design or logging requirements the finding evidences, applied to the agent as a non-human service identity. Only the inactive or frozen run-as user finding is evidence; the inventory finding itself is informational.

agent-monitoring-coverage.scfReason: Active agents with no confirmed Event Monitoring capture and no Transaction Security policy: agent activity may not be logged (unconfirmed where the event log is not readable) and has no real-time intervention.

hsup.reason: Applies when the Event Monitoring log is readable and holds no files while agents are active, so agent activity is not 'logged and stored as per the organisation's logging and auditing requirements'. Where the log was not accessible to the audit, logging is unconfirmed rather than absent.

nzismDirect.reason: Event logging: the readable event log holds no files while agents are active, so agent activity is not logged.
The readable event log of this public cloud service holds no files while agents are active, so its logging capability is not in use.

agent-monitoring-coverage.note: HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI and has no agent-specific requirement; the cited ids are the general access, design or logging requirements the finding evidences, applied to the agent as a non-human service identity. The none finding also fires when the event log is not accessible to the audit user (accessible === false); the finding id cannot separate that case, so the HSUP61, 16.6 and 23.5 citations are unconfirmed when the detail says the log was not accessible.

agent-outbound-actions.scfReason: Agent actions send data out of the org (email, Slack, external services, MCP) without user confirmation, showing no human approval gate on high-risk agent actions and no control over external data transfer.

hsup.reason: Agent actions sending data out by email, Slack, external services or MCP with no user confirmation breach the data leakage guidance that sharing outside the organisation needs 'approval ... sought and documented'.

nzismDirect.reason: Unconfirmed agent sends are data transfers out of the system with no approval step.

agent-outbound-actions.note: HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI and has no agent-specific requirement; the cited ids are the general access, design or logging requirements the finding evidences, applied to the agent as a non-human service identity. The HSUP55 statement covers leakage 'by individuals, systems, or services', so it applies to an agent directly; only the guidance's approval wording assumes a human sender.

agent-query-reach.scfReason: Agents carry the General CRM topic or Query Records action, letting an injected prompt query any object the run-as user can read, so agent data access is not restricted and prompt injection has an open path.

hsup.reason: The General CRM topic or Query Records action lets the agent query any object the run-as user can read rather than what the task needs, contrary to least privilege in the access rights guidance.

nzismDirect.reason: Open-ended query reach over everything the run-as user can read is a system access least-privilege gap, the same basis SCF gives agent-user-privilege.

agent-query-reach.note: HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI and has no agent-specific requirement; the cited ids are the general access, design or logging requirements the finding evidences, applied to the agent as a non-human service identity. The agent-query-reach-unmapped finding reports Query Records on topics not tied to any agent and asserts no exposure; HSUP35 and 16.2 apply only to the per-agent HIGH finding, but the scope prefix cannot separate the two ids.

agent-user-privilege.scfReason: Agent run-as users hold Modify/View All Data, write access to many objects or read access to sensitive objects, so agents do not operate with least privilege and can reach sensitive data beyond their task.

hsup.reason: Modify All Data or View All Data on an agent run-as user is a privileged right held by a software service; the statement requires 'only authorised users, software components and services are provided with privileged access rights' and the guidance ties this to least privilege.
Broad object write access and read access to sensitive objects beyond the agent's task show access is not 'provided using the principle of least privilege'.

agent-user-privilege.note: HISO 10029.4:2025 predates agentic AI and has no agent-specific requirement; the cited ids are the general access, design or logging requirements the finding evidences, applied to the agent as a non-human service identity.

hsup.reason: HSUP36: "only authorised users, software components and services are provided with privileged access rights"; non-admin users who executed anonymous Apex hold the ability to run arbitrary code in production outside change control.

apex-crud-fls.scfReason: Apex performs DML/SOQL without CRUD/FLS checks or with SYSTEM_MODE, bypassing object and field access enforcement.

apex-logging.scfReason: Apex that logs sensitive values exposes regulated data in logs, and System.debug-only code shows no persistent, structured application logging was built in.

hsup.reason: HSUP55: "detect and prevent data leakage through the unauthorised disclosure ... of information by individuals, systems, or services"; Apex writing sensitive values into logs discloses them to anyone who can read those logs.

code-security.scfReason: Apex with SOQL injection patterns shows untrusted input reaching queries without validation or sanitization, a flaw static analysis should have caught and remediated.

hsup.reason: HSUP42 guidance: "security controls and mechanisms are in place to protect against the OWASP top ten" and "reduce or limit exploitations and injection of malicious code"; SOQL injection is an OWASP top ten injection flaw.

HSUP14: "Information systems are securely designed, and appropriate controls are implemented"; guidance: "identify and assess potential threats because of the introduced code". Deployed Apex concatenating input into dynamic SOQL lacks that control.

nzismDirect.reason: 14.5.8.C.01: follow OWASP guidance for building secure web applications; Apex SOQL injection is the injection class that guidance addresses.

14.4.5.C.01: secure programming practices including validating all inputs; 14.4.6.C.01: software reviewed or tested for vulnerabilities before production use. Apex concatenating input into dynamic SOQL fails both.

code-security.note: Org-wide code coverage reflects test-run history rather than code security, so HSUP14, HSUP42, 14.4 and 14.5 apply to the SOQL injection finding only.

connected-app-inactivity.scfReason: Connected apps with no OAuth logins in 90 days are integration access that is no longer tied to a live business process but was never reviewed out or removed.
